correctness.rationale: For all finite fields, path concatenation gives the stated two graded commutator equations and the exact 8-by-8 block matrix. Conjugation centralizers are precisely kernels of the linear commutator map, including in characteristic two. The case partition by the support of four arrow coefficients is disjoint and exhaustive. For a=0 the parity blocks reduce the problem to the ranks of a 2-by-2 matrix; for nonzero independent supports the two ranks are 2 and the compatibility inclusion holds; for adjacent supports both ranks are 3 and L_b(a)=-B_a(b) proves compatibility. Counting all four rank strata and multiplying central-coordinate choices gives the complete polynomial, and the normalization sum of class sizes equals q^12. Direct length-two-path witnesses give odd exponents 1 (n=3) and 3 (all n>=5). Compiled standalone checker independently exhausts q=2,3,5 and returns VERIFY_OK. The proof, rather than these finite tests, establishes all prime powers.

originality.rationale: Earlier literature introduces algebra groups and supercharacters (Diaconis–Thiem), reduces class/character counts to commutator rank data under conditions (O'Brien–Voll), and establishes class-size graph polynomials for nilpotency-class-two graphical groups (Rossmann). Those antecedents do not calculate the class-three ordinary conjugacy polynomial of a fourth-truncated four-cycle radical, and the graphical-group formula cannot imply it because triple commutators are nonzero. A previous local square-zero-element classification of the same Nakayama algebras computes a different invariant, not ordinary conjugacy classes. Targeted published-finding corpus searches for cyclic Nakayama algebra groups, class-size exponents and adjacency commutator ranks found no exact or dominating counterpart. Residual risk from Robinson 1998 and unindexed specialized work remains.

value.rationale: The class-size polynomial is the complete natural conjugacy-class distribution of the principal unipotent group of the first four-vertex oriented cyclic Nakayama algebra of Loewy length four. It determines its class number and every conjugacy orbit size in arbitrary characteristic, and the all-cycle parity obstruction shows the striking even-power spectrum is a structurally isolated resonance, not an arbitrary small-field numerical coincidence. This is a nontrivial class-three complement to the mature class-two graphical-group enumerations, without claiming general higher-cycle classification.
